title: A Seat above the Quay
story: The noon bus passed Idris without stopping, because roadworks had removed any safe place for a request stop at Maren Quay. His ticket named a guesthouse that would hold his room only until dusk. The later driver's sheet already listed every seat as taken. A supervisor radioed ahead and learned that a passenger had relinquished one seat in the town before the headland. The seat was his only if he accepted a drop at the crossroads above the quay, not at the harbour gate, and then walked for twenty minutes. Idris accepted, because a refusal meant a night in the hut and a forfeited first night at the guesthouse. The driver validated the old ticket and annotated the new drop in the margin. He kept that ticket in case the guesthouse asked why he had arrived on foot and after dark. The compromise cost him a downhill walk, yet it preserved the booking.

Lost because a condition was not met.
Added a short written note to a document.

quiz.question: Where did Idris agree to leave the later bus?
options: At the crossroads above the quay
At the harbour gate
Inside the supervisor's hut
In the town before the headland
quiz.correctAnswer: At the crossroads above the quay
quiz.explanation: The only free seat required him to get off at the crossroads above the quay.
quiz.supportingSentence: The seat was his only if he accepted a drop at the crossroads above the quay, not at the harbour gate, and then walked for twenty minutes.

quiz.question: What did the driver write in the margin of the old ticket?
options: The new drop
A full cash refund
The guesthouse telephone number
A complaint about the roadworks
quiz.explanation: The driver annotated the new drop in the margin after validating the ticket.
quiz.supportingSentence: The driver validated the old ticket and annotated the new drop in the margin.

quiz.question: Why could a late arrival put the room booking at risk?
options: The guesthouse had to hold the room only until dusk
Walking on the quay was banned after sunset
Paper tickets were wiped clean at noon
The hut refused every guest who carried a case
quiz.correctAnswer: The guesthouse had to hold the room only until dusk
quiz.explanation: The ticket said the room would be held only until dusk, so a later arrival was unprotected.
quiz.supportingSentence: His ticket named a guesthouse that would hold his room only until dusk.

quiz.question: What does forfeited mean in this passage?
options: Lost because a required condition was missed
Moved into a room beside the harbour
Paid for a second time by the driver
Locked inside the hut until morning
quiz.correctAnswer: Lost because a required condition was missed
quiz.explanation: Refusing the seat would have meant losing the first night at the guesthouse.
quiz.supportingSentence: Idris accepted, because a refusal meant a night in the hut and a forfeited first night at the guesthouse.

quiz.question: Why does the writer mention the roadworks?
options: To explain why the noon bus could not stop for him
To recommend a different coast for a holiday
To show that Idris was repairing the road
To prove the guesthouse had moved inland
quiz.correctAnswer: To explain why the noon bus could not stop for him
quiz.explanation: The roadworks had removed any safe place for the noon bus to stop.
quiz.supportingSentence: The noon bus passed Idris without stopping, because roadworks had removed any safe place for a request stop at Maren Quay.
